### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/permission.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/permission.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9079825bbc3c51597e19b7329fbf6e9e06a4736c` — the merge of head `68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb` into base `78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9079825bbc3c51597e19b7329fbf6e9e06a4736c && git checkout 9079825bbc3c51597e19b7329fbf6e9e06a4736c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0 68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb && git checkout -B drift-repro 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0 && git merge --no-ff 68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36085 · head `68d5bb9762` · **ACCEPT** · 2026-11-21T13:48Z

Card #36050, step 2 of #34365. Claim 7062072947, corrected in place: `docs/adr` was taken out of the surface and `identity/eval-user.zod.ts` was added. Reports 7062809571 and 7063562451. I read the whole diff against `8145424b53`, 28 files, +488/−22. The PR declares Clause-② yes (widening) and Metadata-protocol added, with Skills-docs following in #36053.

### What holds
- **The spec key** (`permission.zod.ts`) is `viewAllFields: z.boolean().optional()` and has no default, so an entry that omits it parses without the key. A runtime built before the key never meets a materialized key it would refuse. The key also rides the wire `EffectiveObjectPermission`. `AccessMatrixEntrySchema` gains an optional column.
- **One vote, both merges.** `superuserFieldVote` (core) now reads `holdsViewAllFields` beside View All. It applies the same own-row rule (`declaresOwnReadMask` → no read vote) and returns `{ readable: true, editable: false }`, so it casts no edit vote. `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` and `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions`, which feeds `/auth/me/permissions`, both go through it, so the two merges cannot disagree. `holdsViewAllFields` takes the same `objects[name] || objects['*']` lookup as `holdsSuperuserBypass`, and it is deliberately **not** a disjunct of it, so RLS, sharing, explain, posture and `readable-ids` stay on the record axis. I checked the other `viewAllRecords` readers outside the diff: the `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula`, the RLS and CBP filters, the posture ladder and the tenant layer 0. They are all record-axis, and none casts a field vote.
- **Every reader of the super-user bits learns it:**
  - the agent ceiling clears it (`AGENT_CEILING_OBJECT_KEYS`);
  - the delegated-admin gate's condition (a) refuses it on `'*'`, with its own wording;
  - `describeHighPrivilegeBits` flags it on any object, so it is refused at the audience anchors;
  - the access-matrix column is written only when `true`, and its diff reads an absent bit as `false`;
  - the lint rollup-visibility walker documents why the bit neither lifts an own-row hide nor makes a `'*'` cover a private object.
- **The built-in sets answer as before.**
  - `organization_admin` and `admin_full_access` carry the bit on `'*'` beside VAMA. A table of pins (each set × companion × both merges) shows the same answer with the bit as without it.
  - `deriveWallLessOrgAdmin` drops it along with the two bypass bits. A control pin shows the bit **would** change that variant's answer, which is why it is dropped.
- **Pins assert behaviour.** Covered:
  - reading alone, read-only, by the object entry and by `'*'`;
  - an own `readable: false` beats the set's own bit, while another set's bit still reads the field;
  - an explicit `editable: false` stays an edit lock;
  - an explicit object entry is the set's whole answer, so the wildcard bit does not reach it;
  - no row-level bypass;
  - audience-anchor refusal, with a control on an explicit `false`;
  - the boundary wording;
  - byte-identical matrix rows.
- **Changeset.** I checked it sentence by sentence. The bumps are `minor` on spec, core, plugin-security and lint, which is what `Metadata-protocol: added` requires on the packages it moves.
- **CI at `68d5bb9762`:** 62 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure. Check Changeset finished green after its re-run.

### For the L2, my reading of the open point (not blocking L1)
A `'*'` `viewAllFields` also votes on the fields of **private-posture** objects. `holdsViewAllFields` takes `'*'` with no private-posture check, while `resolveObjectPermission` (ADR-0066 D2) lets a plain `'*'` reach a private object only when it carries a bypass bit.
- **Effect:** a set `{ '*': { allowRead, viewAllFields } }` grants no access to a private object P. But once another set grants read on P and hides a field there, this set's `'*'` reads that field anyway. The field vote reaches an object the entry's own object grant does not cover.
- **Blast radius today:** only a platform administrator can author or bind such a set. Condition (a) keeps organization administrators out, and the high-privilege check keeps the `everyone` and `guest` anchors out.
- **My lean:** mirror the private-posture rule in `holdsViewAllFields`. A `'*'` bit should vote on a private object only when that wildcard also carries `viewAllRecords` or `modifyAllRecords`. The built-in admin sets carry both bypass bits on `'*'`, so they are unaffected now and after the later major.

The ruling belongs to the L2 (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER: published schema face).

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1.** The changeset's "Nothing behaves differently yet." holds for every stack that exists today. A newly authored bit on a set without VAMA *does* cast a new vote, which the first paragraph says. Writing "Nothing that exists today behaves differently yet" would make the two paragraphs agree.
- **N2.** The Studio permission matrix (`ui/…/permission-slice.ts`) does not model the key. It carries it through save untouched (its index-signature rule), so nothing is lost, but there is no way to author it in the UI. That belongs with the #36053 follow-up or its own card.

### Owed
- **CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 (Fable):** the face is the published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`), and it should rule on the private-posture point above.
- **Tier H, via the seat** after the L2.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-clamp.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/lint/src/build-access-matrix.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts, packages/spec/liveness/permission.json

PR #36085 for card #36050 (step 2 of #34365, ruling of record 6912661484). Read: the card and its four comments, the parent ruling, the PR body, the net diff of 28 files, and the check-runs on this head (62 success, 12 skipped, none failed or pending). The cited code was read in the tree at this head. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies:

- **Authoring: `ObjectPermissionSchema` accepts `viewAllFields`, a boolean, optional, no default** — right. An entry that omits it parses without the key, so no existing artifact changes shape.
- **Wire: `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` carries the key, and `/auth/me/permissions` echoes `viewAllFields: true` on `objects['*']` for holders of the two admin sets** — right. That schema strips unknown keys, so an older client ignores it. The super-user fold and the plain-wildcard coverage copy grant bits only, so no per-object entry gains the key from a wildcard.
- **Field merges: a set carrying the bit on the object (its own entry, else `'*'`) casts a read vote on every field the merge holds, never an edit vote, and no read vote on a field its own row declares `readable: false`** — right. One function, `superuserFieldVote`, answers for both merges. Its two callers that pass no field name read `.editable` only, so the new non-null answer changes nothing for them.
- **Not widened: `holdsSuperuserBypass`, `resolveObjectPermission`, `objectPermissionGrants`, the admin posture** — right. The bit grants no verb, no record and no posture. Core reads only `systemPermissions` from the platform-admin declaration.
- **Built-in sets: `admin_full_access` and `organization_admin` carry it on `'*'`; `organization_admin_no_bypass` drops it** — right. On those two wildcards the record bits already cast the same vote, and the variant never held it.
- **Audience anchors refuse a set carrying it on any entry** (`describeHighPrivilegeBits`, and through it the `security-anchor-high-privilege` lint) — right. It is checked after system permissions and the record bits, so every existing set gets the same answer in the same words.
- **Organization boundary, condition (a), refuses it on `'*'`; a per-object bit stays inside** — right. The three built-in admin sets are refused by name before (a) is read.
- **Agent ceiling clears it and counts it a breach** — right. Today the ceiling removes the same field vote by clearing the record bits.
- **Access matrix: an optional column written only when `true`; the diff compares bits as booleans and names the new one** — right. The compile gate fails on the semantic diff, so without the label a set gaining the bit would pass unreviewed.
- **Not changed: `security-wildcard-vama` accepts a package-authored `'*'` that carries only `viewAllFields`** — not right as left. See ③.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/lint` — right. Those are the four packages the diff moves, and `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on each.

`Clause-②: yes` (PR body) and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (changeset) match the diff: one key on two schemas and one optional column added, nothing removed or narrowed. The new refusals bind only a set that carries the new key, which no set could carry before. `Check Changeset` is green. The changeset text is one fact short (N1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1, extend the surface to `eval-user.zod.ts`** — answered A by the seat on the claim, and landed. Verified in the tree.
- **Q2, does a `'*'` `viewAllFields` vote on the fields of private-posture objects** (report 7062809571, and the PR body's "For the contract review" paragraph) — answered: **A holds.** It votes there, as built.
  1. Field votes are already posture-blind. `getFieldPermissions` counts every `fields` row keyed on the object, with no check that the row's set grants the object or that its wildcard covers it. A set with no say on a private object can already re-open one of its fields with an explicit `readable: true` row. The wildcard bit adds breadth, not a new kind of reach.
  2. ADR-0066's precedence list makes the private posture a gate on the caller (step 1), then combines field grants across the caller's sets within the gates (step 2).
  3. The ruling separates the axes. Under B, the field reach on a private object would depend on whether the same wildcard carries a record bit, so after step 3 View All would again decide field visibility there.
  4. The bit grants no object access (pinned), and the three binding gates in ① treat `'*'` plus the bit as super-user class.

  Against A: ADR-0066 D2's heading speaks of opting a private object "out of blanket wildcard grants", and this is the first key on a plain `'*'` that reaches one. I read D2's operative sentence (about `allowRead` and access) and the precedence list as the governing text. B would therefore be a new rule, and the maintainer's to make. It is free to change until the first release that carries the key, and a narrowing after it.
- **Dev flag: `security-wildcard-vama` does not read the new bit, reported "carrier: none"** — that disposition is wrong. The PR body files the rule under "record-scope only", but this PR's own gates call a `'*'` `viewAllFields` "the field half of the superuser wildcard". A package can author it with no finding, and it reaches every other package's objects. A card is owed before the key ships: a sub-card of #34365, or #36052 widened. Error or warning is that card's question. No change to this head.
- **Dev flag: the `/auth/me/permissions` echo** — accepted as additive (see ①). It belongs in the changeset (N1).
- **Card item 5, the ADR-0066 D2 ⑧ note** — not in the diff. The claim routes it to the ADR revisions card as a `carrier:` note at ACCEPT, which the landing rules allow. No comment on the card or the PR carries that note yet. It should name the four texts the code now extends (ADR-0066 D2 ⑧, the ADR-0090 D5 anchor list, ADR-0090 D12 condition (a), the ADR-0151 D3 ceiling) and state the private-object reach of Q2, so the maintainer sees it when that text lands.
- **Deviations** — Model-free commit trailers are the repository's rule. `test:repo` and three gate families were not run locally; the check-runs on this head are the verdicts, and all are green. The `app-showcase` snapshot was not measured, but the one new write is guarded by `=== true` and no file under `examples/` authors the key.
- **SQL push-down** — nothing to flag. The vote is a fold over sets already resolved; the diff adds no query, id list or join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **`permission.zod.ts`** — holds against the ruling and its first consumer. Every rule the jsdoc and the description state is true of `superuserFieldVote` and `holdsViewAllFields`: a read vote, no edit vote, the own-row rule, own entry else `'*'`, no object access, optional with no default (one loose sentence is N2). A field's `requiredPermissions` gate folds after the merge, so the bit never lifts it, as the ruling's sensitivity tiers require.
- **`eval-user.zod.ts`** — holds. The only reader of the declaration's `objects` is the `admin_full_access` spread, and the no-behaviour-change pin compares the shipped set with and without the bit on both merges.
- **`high-privilege.ts`** — holds. Per-object and wildcard are both refused, the class of the record bits it sits beside.
- **`explain.zod.ts`** — holds against its first consumer, `buildAccessMatrix`.
- **Implementing files** — each agrees with the contract.
  - `effective-object-permissions.ts`: View All and the new bit share the own-row check, and Modify All still returns first.
  - `default-permission-sets.ts`: the variant's derivation drops the bit, with a control pin showing the bit would change its answer.
  - `agent-ceiling-clamp.ts`, `delegated-admin-gate.ts`: as judged in ①.
  - `validate-rollup-source-visibility.ts`: comments only, and correct. That rule judges one set alone, where the own row beats the own bit.
  - `permission-evaluator.ts`: jsdoc only, true of the code.
  - `liveness/permission.json`: `live`, and its anchors resolve (`Spec property liveness` is green).

Tried, and it held: an explicit entry without the bit beside a wildcard with it casts no vote. The bit beside Modify All and an own mask leaves Modify All winning, as ruled until step 3. On a delegated request the two masks intersect and the agent's side is clamped. An explicit `false` leaves a matrix snapshot byte-identical.

Nits, none of which changes behaviour:

- **N1 (nit)** — The changeset's second paragraph names `organization_admin` only. Since the patch round `admin_full_access` carries the bit too, through `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` (a `@objectstack/spec` export), and both holders get the echo on `objects['*']`. "Nothing behaves differently yet" is true of every set that exists, not of a set that newly authors the bit alone. Fix it on the changeset, a prose face. The liveness row's note has the same omission: accepted, to be corrected when the row is next touched.
- **N2 (nit)** — In `permission.zod.ts`, "on a set that carries either bit this key changes nothing" is exact per entry, not per set. The `FieldPermissionSchema` docblock in the same file still names the declaring sets and the super-user sets as the only voters. Accepted deviations; fold them into #36053 or step 3.
- **N3 (nit)** — The private-object reach of Q2 is contract, but only the jsdoc says it ("every object the set does not name explicitly"). The published description says "Allowed on the '*' entry", and no test pins it. Follow-up: one pin on both merges, and one sentence in the teaching card #36053.

## Contract review brief — PR #36085 @ `68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb` (card #36050)

`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36050: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #36085: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb`
  · the check-runs on `68d5bb976287da873b5e85edd3f82ba1155bc0fb`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/77e29ae5-1571-5694-8c73-05987461330b/scratchpad/pr-36085/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
